headline: 英國藝文本週三則新評
context: 英國藝文圈本週有三則新評論。愛丁堡藝穗節推出遊戲式劇場作品《Ten Ways to Die Happy》，觀眾被邀請親身體驗一場人生思想實驗：把人生時間具象成一盤盤花朵、投入水池，用完就代表「死亡」。改編自安德魯・歐哈根（Andrew O'Hagan）小說的舞台劇《Mayflies》，在愛丁堡一處倉庫重現一九八六年曼徹斯特傳奇夜店Haçienda的氛圍。作家湯姆・紐蘭茲（Tom Newlands）的新書《Something Like Happiness》，描寫一對蘇格蘭年輕夫妻，在破敗的公寓裡照顧自閉症兒子的艱難日常。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Underbelly, Bristo Square, Edinburgh Audience members are invited to examine what they will do with their lives in this earnest shared thought experiment If you could hold the years of your life in your hands like coins, would you choose to spend them differently? This is the thoughtful, earnest tone of Ten Ways to Die Happy, an existential but somewhat formulaic Italian production (performed here in English) created by Emanuele Aldrovandi and Jacopo Giacomoni. In this gentle gameshow, we are asked not just to consider how we would use the finite time we have, but to put this thought experiment into practice. Eight people are plucked at random from the audience. My number is called, so I don a white robe, choose a new name for my new life, and take a seat on stage. Perla Ambrosini is our ethereal host, standing in fabric armour in a shallow pool of water. Each of us has a tray of flowers that we throw into the pool, every plastic bud representing the “energy” available to invest in work, art and family. Once our supply is up, we’re dead. At Underbelly, Bristo Square, Edinburgh , until 31 August All our Edinburgh festival reviews Continue reading...
sources.title: Ten Ways to Die Happy review – gameshow invites you to don a robe and treasure time

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Rear Warehouse, Brown’s of Leith, Edinburgh Two men look back on their hedonistic past from a sobering present in Grid Iron’s adaptation of Andrew O’Hagan’s novel The site-specific specialists at Edinburgh’s Grid Iron company could have gone for a number of locations to suit an adaptation of Andrew O’Hagan’s semi-autobiographical novel . Perhaps a squalid mid-80s flat to match the formative years of Jimmy Collins, the book’s narrator, and Tully Dawson, his lifelong best friend. Or a caravan park to reflect their Ayrshire holiday escape. More poignantly, they could have found a clinic to echo the novel’s slow journey to Dignitas, where the grownup Tully chooses to end his life after a terminal cancer diagnosis. Instead, adapter and director Ben Harrison has homed in on the book’s central motif: the teenage trip in 1986 to Manchester’s G-Mex for the Festival of the Tenth Summer followed by a night in the Haçienda. That brings us to a warehouse in Leith, to evoke the flavour of that Thatcher-era moment when heavy industry transitioned to the leisure economy. At Rear Warehouse, Brown’s of Leith, Edinburgh , until 30 August All our Edinburgh festival reviews Continue reading...
sources.title: Mayflies review – Manchester’s Haçienda roars back to life in an Edinburgh warehouse

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: A twentysomething Scottish couple care for their autistic son in the bleak follow-up to Only Here, Only Now Frazer and Caitlin have been emotionally entwined since schooldays. Now in their mid-20s, and parents of a five-year-old, they live in a grotty flat in a Scottish new town – the faded posters read “Happiness, Here” – that has crumbled into decay. Jobs are scarce and unrewarding; little Jamie, who has autism, is silent; and the pressure is starting to tell. Frazer’s adored Caitlin is “beautiful and driven”, fit, petite – and a rageaholic. At her mildest she’s irritated and unreasonable, at her worst violent and intimidating. She is incensed at Frazer’s refusal to move from their mould-infested block to the new council house they’ve been assigned. Apex Court is where he was brought up, filled with relics of his dead parents, and it’s the only home his son has ever known. “You’ve become the sad sack guardian of a bunch of shite that belonged to your parents, including their hovel of a flat,” Cait sneers. Continue reading...

thread_text:
英國藝文圈本週有三則新評論。

愛丁堡藝穗節推出遊戲式劇場《Ten Ways to Die Happy》，觀眾被邀請親身體驗一場人生思想實驗：把人生時間具象成一盤盤花朵，投入水池，用完就代表「死亡」。改編自安德魯・歐哈根（Andrew O'Hagan）小說的舞台劇《Mayflies》，在愛丁堡一處倉庫重現一九八六年曼徹斯特傳奇夜店Haçienda的氛圍，描寫兩名老友從縱情青春走向清醒中年。作家湯姆・紐蘭茲（Tom Newlands）的新書《Something Like Happiness》，描寫一對蘇格蘭年輕夫妻，在破敗的公寓裡照顧自閉症兒子的艱難日常。

—— 本則整理自 The Guardian 於 2026 年 8 月 12 日發佈的報導，讓圖書館員翻譯給你聽。

voice_text: 英國藝文圈，本週有三則新評論。愛丁堡藝穗節，有一齣遊戲式劇場作品，讓觀眾親身體驗一場人生思想實驗——把人生時間具象成一盤盤花朵，投入水池，用完就代表「死亡」。還有一齣舞台劇，改編自安德魯・歐哈根的小說，在愛丁堡一處倉庫，重現了一九八六年曼徹斯特傳奇夜店Haçienda的氛圍，講兩個老友從縱情青春，走向清醒中年。還有一本新書，出自作家湯姆・紐蘭茲，寫的是一對蘇格蘭年輕夫妻，在破敗的公寓裡，照顧自閉症兒子的艱難日常。
